drug_class: Tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) / VEGF receptor blocker / Targeted cancer therapy
purpose: Tivozanib is used to treat advanced kidney cancer (renal cell carcinoma) in adults. It is typically used in patients who have already tried other treatments that did not work or stopped working. It helps slow down or stop the growth and spread of cancer cells.
how_it_works: Cancer tumors need to grow new blood vessels to survive and spread — this process is called angiogenesis. Tivozanib blocks special proteins called VEGF receptors that cancer cells use to build these new blood vessels. By cutting off this blood supply, the drug starves the tumor and helps prevent it from growing or spreading.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include high blood pressure, feeling very tired, diarrhea, loss of appetite, nausea, hoarse voice or voice changes, swelling in the hands or feet, low thyroid levels, headache, and skin or hair color changes. Most side effects can be managed, so always let your doctor or pharmacist know how you are feeling.
warnings: Tivozanib can cause serious high blood pressure, which needs to be monitored closely. It may increase the risk of heart problems, blood clots, stroke, or bleeding. It can harm an unborn baby, so women who could become pregnant must use effective birth control during treatment and for at least one month after stopping. Avoid breastfeeding while taking this medication. Tell your doctor about all other medications you take, as some drugs can interact with tivozanib. Do not take it if you are pregnant.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is one 1.34 mg capsule taken by mouth once a day for 21 days in a row, followed by a 7-day break (no medication). This 28-day cycle is then repeated. Take it at the same time each day, with or without food. Swallow the capsule whole — do not crush or open it. If you miss a dose and there are more than 12 hours until your next scheduled dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is less than 12 hours, skip the missed dose and continue your regular schedule.
